items.title: 6.2.3 Equation of Normal to a Circle at P(x1, y1) (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Book p. 175-176: 6.2.3 normal xy1 - yx1 = 0 to x^2 + y^2 = r^2; Note box; Example 10 (book prints x = +-2 for (x - 2)^2 = 0)

blocks.text: Tangent ke baad ab normal ki baari hai. Yaad kijiye: normal woh line hai jo point of contact par tangent ke perpendicular ho. Pichle sabaqon mein hum ne dekha ke circle ka tangent radius par perpendicular hota hai. Is ka seedha nateeja yeh hai ke circle ka normal radius wali line hi hai, yani woh hamesha centre se guzarta hai. Is sabaq mein isi baat ko equation ki shakal mein dekhenge aur ek misaal hal karenge.

Circle \(x^{2} + y^{2} = r^{2}\) ke point \(P(x_{1}, y_{1})\) par tangent \(xx_{1} + yy_{1} = r^{2}\) hai. Normal yeh hai:
\[xy_{1} - yx_{1} = 0 \quad \text{ya} \quad \dfrac{x}{x_{1}} = \dfrac{y}{y_{1}}\]

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text: Circle ka centre \((0, 0)\) normal ki equation ko poora karta hai. Is se tasdeeq hoti hai ke circle ka normal hamesha us ke centre se guzarta hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yeh \(xy_{1} - yx_{1} = 0\) aaya kahan se? Kitab seedha likh deti hai, hum qadam ba qadam dekhte hain. Tangent ka slope \(-\frac{x_{1}}{y_{1}}\) tha, to normal ka slope us ka ulta aur sign badla hua, yani \(\frac{y_{1}}{x_{1}}\). Ab \(P(x_{1}, y_{1})\) se point-slope form:
\[y - y_{1} = \dfrac{y_{1}}{x_{1}}(x - x_{1})\]
Dono taraf \(x_{1}\) se zarb dein:
\[x_{1}y - x_{1}y_{1} = xy_{1} - x_{1}y_{1}\]
\(-x_{1}y_{1}\) dono taraf hai, cancel ho gaya:
\[xy_{1} - yx_{1} = 0\]
Form \(\frac{x}{x_{1}} = \frac{y}{y_{1}}\) ke liye \(x_{1} \ne 0\) aur \(y_{1} \ne 0\) chahiye (zero se taqseem nahin ho sakti), lekin \(xy_{1} - yx_{1} = 0\) har point par chalta hai. Is liye exam mein yahi form likhna behtar hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
General circle \(x^{2} + y^{2} + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0\) ke liye (yeh hamari taraf se izafa hai): point \(P(x_{1}, y_{1})\) par normal woh line hai jo \(P\) aur centre \(C(-g, -f)\) ko milati hai. Two-point form se:
\[(x - x_{1})(y_{1} + f)\]
\[- (y - y_{1})(x_{1} + g) = 0\]
Aksar yahi sab se tez tareeqa hota hai: bas point ko centre se jor do. Jaise kisi pahiye (wheel) ki spoke hamesha beech se kinare tak jati hai, waise hi normal centre se point tak jata hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Yeh misaal kitab ki nahin. Circle \(x^{2} + y^{2} = 25\) par point \((3, 4)\) par normal nikaliye.
Formula \(xy_{1} - yx_{1} = 0\) mein \(x_{1} = 3\), \(y_{1} = 4\) rakhiye:
\[4x - 3y = 0\]
Tasdeeq: \((3, 4)\) rakhne se \(12 - 12 = 0\), aur \((0, 0)\) rakhne se bhi zero. Yani line point se bhi guzarti hai aur centre se bhi. 6.2.1 mein isi point par tangent \(3x + 4y = 25\) tha; dono ke slopes \(\frac{4}{3}\) aur \(-\frac{3}{4}\) ka product \(-1\) hai.

Ab kitab ki misaal ki taraf chalte hain. Is sawal mein ek chhoti si mushkil hai: point poora nahin diya, sirf us ka ordinate (\(y\) wali value) diya hai. Is liye pehla kaam point dhoondna hai; us ke baad tangent aur normal bilkul seedhe hain. Har qadam ke saath dekhte jaiye ke kaun sa rule kaam aa raha hai.

blocks.title: Example 10
blocks.problem: Find the equation of the tangent and normal to the circle \(x^{2} + y^{2} - 4x + 6y + 12 = 0\) at the point on the circle whose ordinate is \(-2\).
steps:
Diya gaya: circle \(x^{2} + y^{2} - 4x + 6y + 12 = 0\) aur us par ek point jis ka ordinate (\(y\)-coordinate) \(-2\) hai.
Maloom karna: us point par tangent aur normal ki equations.
Tareeqa: sab se pehle point poora maloom karna hai (sirf \(y\) diya hai, \(x\) nikalna hai). Is ke liye \(y = -2\) circle ki equation mein rakhenge. Phir 6.2.2 wale rule se tangent likhenge, aur aakhir mein normal, jo point se guzarne wali tangent par perpendicular line hai.

Qadam 1: Point ka abscissa (\(x\)-coordinate) nikalna
\(y = -2\) circle ki equation mein rakhte hain:
\[x^{2} + (-2)^{2} - 4x + 6(-2) + 12 = 0\]
\[x^{2} + 4 - 4x - 12 + 12 = 0\]
\[x^{2} - 4x + 4 = 0\]
\[(x - 2)^{2} = 0 \Rightarrow x = 2\]
Kyun: point circle par hai, is liye us ke coordinates circle ki equation ko poora karte hain. \(x^{2} - 4x + 4\) ek perfect square hai, \((x - 2)^{2}\).
Dhyan dein: kitab yahan \(x = \pm 2\) likhti hai, jo ghalat hai (neeche "Kitab ki ghalti" dekhiye). Perfect square zero ho to sirf ek hi (dohra) root hota hai, \(x = 2\). Is dohre root ka matlab hai ke line \(y = -2\) circle ko sirf ek jagah milti hai; yahi ishara hai ke yeh line khud tangent hogi.

Qadam 2: Point of contact
\[x = 2, \quad y = -2\]
Yani point of contact \(P(2, -2)\) hai.
Kyun: tangent ke formula mein \(x_{1} = 2\), \(y_{1} = -2\) rakhne hain, is liye pehle inhein saaf likh liya.

Qadam 3: Rule se tangent likhna
\((x_{1}, y_{1})\) par tangent ki equation:
\[xx_{1} + yy_{1} - 2(x + x_{1})\]
\[+ 3(y + y_{1}) + 12 = 0\]
Kyun: 6.2.2 ka rule: \(-4x \to -4\cdot\frac{x + x_{1}}{2} = -2(x + x_{1})\), \(6y \to 6\cdot\frac{y + y_{1}}{2} = 3(y + y_{1})\), aur constant 12 waisa hi rehta hai.

Qadam 4: \(x_{1} = 2\), \(y_{1} = -2\) rakhna
\[2x + (-2)y - 2(x + 2) + 3(y - 2) + 12 = 0\]
\[2x - 2y - 2x - 4 + 3y - 6 + 12 = 0\]
\[y + 2 = 0\]
Yani tangent ki equation \(y = -2\) hai.
Kyun: brackets khole, phir milte julte terms jore: \(2x - 2x = 0\), \(-2y + 3y = y\), \(-4 - 6 + 12 = 2\). \(x\) wale terms khatam ho gaye, matlab tangent ek horizontal line hai.

Qadam 5: Normal
Tangent \(y = -2\) horizontal hai, is liye \(P(2, -2)\) par normal us point se guzarne wali vertical line hai:
\[x = 2\]
Kyun: horizontal line par perpendicular line hamesha vertical hoti hai, aur normal ko point of contact se guzarna hai. Yahan slope wala formula \(-\frac{1}{m_{T}}\) nahin chalta kyun ke \(m_{T} = 0\) hai; seedha shakal dekh kar likha.

Tasdeeq:
\(P(2, -2)\) circle par hai: \(4 + 4 - 8 - 12 + 12 = 0\).
Centre \(C(-g, -f) = C(2, -3)\) aur radius \(\sqrt{4 + 9 - 12} = 1\).
Normal \(x = 2\) centre \(C(2, -3)\) se guzarta hai, jaisa har circle ke normal ko guzarna chahiye.
Centre se tangent \(y = -2\) ka faasla \(|-3 + 2| = 1\) hai, jo radius ke barabar hai. Yani \(y = -2\) waqai circle ko chhooti hai.
blocks.answer: Tangent: \(y + 2 = 0\) (yani \(y = -2\)); normal: \(x = 2\). Point of contact \(P(2, -2)\) hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Example 10 mein kitab \((x - 2)^{2} = 0\) ke baad \(x = \pm 2\) likhti hai. Sahi: \((x - 2)^{2} = 0 \Rightarrow x = 2\), sirf ek (dohra) root. \(x = -2\) rakhne se \(x^{2} - 4x + 4 = 4 + 8 + 4 = 16 \ne 0\), is liye woh root hai hi nahin. Kitab agli line mein khud sahi point \(P(2, -2)\) istemal karti hai, is liye aakhri jawab par koi asar nahin.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Example 10 mein general-circle wala normal formula lagaiye: \(x_{1} = 2\), \(y_{1} = -2\), \(g = -2\), \(f = 3\). Kya aap ko \((x - 2)(1) - (y + 2)(0) = 0\), yani \(x = 2\) mila? Yahi jawab kitab ka bhi hai.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(x^{2} + y^{2} = r^{2}\) ke point \((x_{1}, y_{1})\) par normal: \(xy_{1} - yx_{1} = 0\); yeh origin se guzarta hai.
2. Kisi bhi circle ke kisi point par normal = us point ko centre se milane wali line.
3. Tangent horizontal ho to normal \(x = x_{1}\); tangent vertical ho to normal \(y = y_{1}\).
4. Agar point ki sirf ek coordinate di ho to pehle circle ki equation se doosri coordinate nikaliye.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \((x - 2)^{2} = 0\) se \(x = \pm 2\) likh dena (jaise kitab ne Example 10 mein likha). Square zero ho to sirf ek dohra root hota hai.
2. Normal mein tangent wala slope hi laga dena. Normal ka slope ulta aur sign badla hua hota hai.
3. Yeh bhool jana ke normal ko centre se guzarna chahiye; yeh har jawab ki muft tasdeeq hai.
